 ‘The Terminal List’ Star, Chris Pratt, Proved His ’90s Country Cred to Garth Brooks (& Failed Jimmy Buffett)
 Quinn Eaton · COUNTRY MUSIC · November 20, 2026 Share Prime Video 
 Chris Pratt is a big fan of 90s country music.
 I don’t know about you, but I’m a big fan of the Terminal List star. Everything he’s in, from Parks and Recreation and Guardians of the Galaxy , is top-tier entertainment. And his story from rags to riches is fascinating. If you’ve never heard it, I’ll give you the short version.
 Pratt was living out of a van in Hawaii at the age of 19, and was waiting tables at a Bubba Gump Shrimp restaurant. He wasn’t even really trying to get into acting, yet one fateful day, a director came into the restaurant, was waited on by Pratt, and that director later gave Chris his first role in Hollywood. He’s been in front of the camera ever since, and he’s slowly but surely built quite the fanbase.
 Fans of his will be happy to know that he’s got a great taste in music too.
 During a recent interview on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, Pratt was asked about his appreciation for country music. The action star proudly shared that he was raised on country, and really digs the “Golden Age” in particular:
 “I love country music. I grew up and we had 94.1 KMPS. That was our country radio station in Seattle. I’m a child of the 80s and 90s, so I think my favorite stuff is probably that 90s prime country. Garth Brooks, George Strait, Clint Black.” 
 That’s a strong list of favorite artists right there.
 Pratt says he was once able to meet Garth Brooks, and even had the opportunity to share the stage with him. He remembers it like it was yesterday, and says he was really starstruck in the moment. Amidst it all, Pratt won’t ever forget the test that Garth Brooks ran by him:
 “I’ve had a chance to meet some of them. I actually met Garth Brooks, and got to sing with Garth Brooks… it was an event, and he was being given an award, and I presented the award to him. Then he sang, and it was a surreal moment. He’s truly the best. 
 I was fan-girling. He had his band there and he walked over and started playing the opening chords to ‘Much Too Young (to Feel This Damn Old). He started playing it and then I kind of sang the first part of the lyrics. 
 He looked at me, (nodded), and was like, ‘Alright.’ Like checking to see if I was really a fan.” 
 Chris Pratt passed the test from Garth Brooks.
 He’d go on to tell a story about how a similar situation played out with the late, great Jimmy Buffett. Pratt didn’t do so well when the leader of the Parrot Heads brought the movie star on stage to help him sing a little song he had called “Margaritaville.” Ever heard of it?
 Pratt certainly had, but had maybe oversold his fandom to Buffett… and quickly disappointed Jimmy when he failed to recount the opening lines to “Margaritaville.” Just goes to show that, if you (the reader) are ever fortunate enough to meet one of your musical heroes… be ready to back it up.
